title: Each finished job writes one operations row with its queue wait, lock wait and run time, and kbjob.py stats prints their medians per operation
goal: the executor records one ops row job.run per finished job in the query log's ops store (closed keys: op, exit class, attempt, queued_ms, wait_ms of waiting-lock and waiting-merge, run_ms), through ql_capture as land.step rows are, and kbjob.py stats prints for each operation one line op n=N queued_ms=MEDIAN wait_ms=MEDIAN run_ms=MEDIAN (nearest-rank p95 beside it), so the wait the service removes from a session is measured the same way backlog.py landings measures a landing

run: import sys,os,tempfile,subprocess; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); env=dict(os.environ,CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA=d,CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=os.getcwd(),KB_HOST_LOCK_DIR=d); s=os.path.join(d,"c.sqlite"); kb=lambda *x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--store",s,*x],env=env,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=300); assert kb("submit","check","--name","backlog-check","--no-ensure").returncode==0; assert kb("serve","--once").returncode in (0,1); r=kb("stats"); assert r.returncode==0 and r.stdout.split()[0]=="check" and "run_ms" in r.stdout and "queued_ms" in r.stdout, r

notes: Why: the operator's first ask is to measure the waiting. Today the measure is reconstructed from land.step and land.end rows and the foreground tool-call rows (kb/_querylog/ops, schema in _tools/ql_capture.py; read by backlog.py landings, bl_ops.py:87 step_stats, kbmon mon_*); a job row gives queue wait, lock wait and run time directly, so the before and after of the service is a number: before (2026-11-08, real items 2026-10-02..11-08): land.end ok median 103 s content (p95 1150 s, n=1701) and 430 s code (p95 1784 s, n=133); kbgit.py sync --push step median 29.8 s (p95 176 s); rag eval 18.1 s; siblings median 0.2 s but p95 76 s, max 1081 s; wait-merge p90 240 s; done step p95 29 s; test.run full median 22.0 s (p95 34.6 s, n=3021). Row schema is closed (ql_capture) and the redactor reads it (_tools/test_redact.py names land.step), so the worker adds job.run beside land.step in the same closed-key way and keeps ids and paths out of the row (op, exit class and numbers only). Related: EP-ajw3oywi (the sprint runner measures its own work as redacted operational events) is the family this row belongs to; EP-wqgicmmj (a live console) may show the job queue as a panel later, not here. No test added unless test_redact.py must name the new event (then one line, no new id).
